b1-unit-55.55.1 Danny's blog: the Strange Games:
Danny: The Strange Games. Last weekend Bruno, Rafa and I took a bus to a small town in the mountains for a festival called the Strange Games. Mrs. Lima's cousin Dora, a retired teacher, started it fifteen years ago. Inspired by her students' crazy ideas, she decided to invent sports that anyone can play, no matter how fit they are.
Danny: The first event was suitcase racing. Competitors carrying heavy suitcases run through an obstacle course built to look like an airport: stairs, a security line and a gate that closes after two minutes. Bruno came second. He says it was physically demanding, but I think he just loves running.
Danny: Next was silent soccer, a game played without words. Players who shout, sing or even laugh have to leave the field for two minutes. The referee, wearing headphones and a huge smile, sent off eleven players in the first half. Rafa lasted six minutes.
Danny: My favorite was the hammock relay. Teams of four, lying in hammocks tied between trees, pass a watermelon from one hammock to the next. If it falls, you start again. It sounds pointless, and it is. But the crowd was laughing so hard that nobody cared.
Danny: The last event, umbrella fencing, needs agility and a high tolerance for water: firefighters spray the competitors fighting with umbrellas. I entered, I got very wet, and I lost to a seventy-year-old woman called Lucia.
Danny: Would I go again? Definitely. The best moment wasn't winning or losing. It was seeing a whole town, from teenagers to grandparents, laughing together on a Sunday afternoon.
